results.question: What do the colour keys in the calibration schedule mean?

results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents, specifically [Source 1], [Source 2], and [Source 5], it appears that the color keys in the calibration schedule refer to the status of equipment calibration.

The possible meanings are:

* Okay: The equipment is calibrated and within acceptable limits.
* Not Okay: The equipment is not calibrated or is out of calibration.
* Out of Calibration: The equipment requires recalibration.

These color codes indicate the current status of each piece of equipment, allowing for easy tracking and monitoring of calibration schedules.

results.question: What pre-operation checks must an operator complete at the start of a shift?
results.expected_answer: Pre-Operation (start of shift) checks including machine cleanliness (no ink/dust/debris on rollers/frames) and safety guards in place (all guards/covers properly secured).
results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context, specifically from Source 8: CON-F-01 - OPERATOR MACHINE CHECKLIST.xlsx, Sheet: Sheet1, Section: Sheet1, the pre-operation checks that an operator must complete at the start of a shift are:

1. Machine cleanliness
2. Safety guards in place
3. Rollers and doctor blades
4. Anilox roller condition
5. Plate cylinder and mounting
6. Ink system (chambers, hoses, pumps)
7. Dryer units (hot air/UV)
8. Job settings loaded correctly
9. Register system/calibration
10. Glue system
11. Strapping system

controlled, administered and audited, and subject to central management review; - An internal audit has been conducted on each site within one year prior to certification; - Following the certification, an internal audit shall be carried out on each site within the certification period. The internal audit shall comply with ISO 22000. - Audit findings of the individual sites shall be considered indicative of the entire system and correction shall be implemented accordingly. - For Organizations with 20 sites or less, multi-site sampling is not allowed. Each site must be audited at each activity. FSSC Multi-site sampling is only possible for categories A, E, FI, G and for organizations with more than 20 sites operating similar processes within these categories. Where multi-site sampling is permitted the following apply; - A sampling plan shall be utilized to ensure an effective audit of the FSMS - The sampling plan for more than 20 sites shall be at the ration of 1 site per 5 sites with a minimum of 20. - The sites shall be randomly selected and after the audit, non-sampled sites may be nonconforming (i.e. not meeting certification thresholds for ISO 22000). - Evaluation of the audit findings of the sampled sites shall be deemed equivalent to the internal audit findings of the same site. - At least annually, an audit of the central FSMS shall be performed - At least annually, surveillance audits shall be performed on the required number of sampled sites. results.question: What are the criteria for disqualifying a supplier?
results.expected_answer: Lack of prompt response to an identified complaint/problem; and failure to supply quality raw material in two successions without corrective action.
results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context, the criteria for disqualifying a supplier are:

1. Lack of prompt response to complaint or problem identified by the suppliers.
2. Lack of supply of quality raw material in two successive instances without corrective actions.

These criteria are mentioned in Source 6: Current HACCP MANUAL 3.10.2022 - Copy.xlsx, Sheet: MGT OF PURCH MAT & SERV, Section: MGT OF PURCH MAT & SERV under the PRP (Food Safety) for Management of Purchased Materials and Services.

results.question: How is waste segregated and disposed of on site?
results.expected_answer: Waste categorised as plastic/PE film, general waste, and liquid waste; segregated daily; PE/trim/flexible film bagged; bins emptied at least once per shift or when full; liquid waste to septic tank cleared by 3rd-party contractor; labelled materials shredded before disposal.
results.ollama_answer:
According to Source 3: Current HACCP MANUAL 3.10.2022 - Copy.xlsx, Sheet: WASTE DISPOSAL, Section: WASTE DISPOSAL, the following procedure is followed for waste segregation and disposal:

1. Waste materials are identified, collected, removed, and disposed of in a manner that prevents contamination of products and production areas.
2. The types of waste generated at Poly Products Ltd are categorized as:
	* Plastic waste-flexible films
	* General waste including packages of consumables, food debris from canteen, and other office supplies
	* Liquid waste from toilet facilities and the main amenities
3. Containers for waste, inedible or hazardous substances, must meet certain standards and guidelines, including:
	* Clearly identified for their various intended purposes
	* Located in designated areas
	* Constructed of impervious material that can be readily cleaned and sanitized
	* Made up of lids that are closed when not in immediate use
4. Waste management and removal procedures include:
	* Liquid waste from toilet facilities and the main amenities is channeled into a septic tank, which is regularly recovered and disposed of by a third-party liquid waste management contractor.
	* Solid waste is segregated on a daily basis into general waste, PE waste for recycling, flexible waste for disfiguration and destruction, trim waste, plastic, and others. The PE, trim waste, and flexible film waste are disposed in plastic bags.
	* A dedicated area at the back of the factory premises has been allocated where all empty drums used in the factory are stored prior to being carted away for disposal.
5. Waste is not allowed to accumulate in product-handling or storage areas. All bins across the site are clearly labelled with the type of waste they carry. Bins positioned at production areas and warehouses are removed at least once per shift or when they are full, whichever comes first.

In summary, waste segregation and disposal on site involve identifying and categorizing different types of waste, using dedicated containers that meet certain standards, and following procedures for managing and removing liquid and solid waste to prevent contamination and ensure a sanitary environment.

results.question: How does the facility control physical contamination from glass and brittle materials?
results.expected_answer: Periodic inspection of Perspex/glass machine coverings, monthly glass audits with corrective actions, and snap-off knife blades are forbidden.
results.ollama_answer:
According to Source 3: Current HACCP MANUAL 3.10.2022 - Copy.xlsx, Sheet: CROSS CONTAMINATION (2), Section: CROSS CONTAMINATION (2), the facility controls physical contamination from glass and brittle materials by:

1. Periodic inspections are done to ensure coverings of machines made of brittle materials such as machine covering made of Perspex and glass components of equipment are intact.
2. Regular monthly glass audits are carried out and measures put in place to prevent, control or detect potential contamination and corrective actions put in place.
3. The use of snap off knife blade is forbidden.
4. Tools are to be locked up in their respective tool boxes and must not be left loose in any place or on surfaces where product contamination can occur.

Additionally, Source 5: Current HACCP MANUAL 3.10.2022 - Copy.xlsx, Sheet: Hazard Analysis, Section: Hazard Analysis, mentions that:

1. Bags of resins are handled individually so that any broken or contaminated bags can easily be identified and segregated.
2. Bags are cleaned before being used.

These measures aim to prevent physical contamination from glass and brittle materials in the facility's processes.

The Job Ticket No and name of the manufacturing facility shall appear on each case and/or pallet of product, including quantity.   7.5 Critical Tracking Events 7.5.1 Considering the entire food supply chain, there are several points in time and locations where data need to be collected to enable full product traceability.  7.5.2 These points have been termed to be “Critical Tracking Events.” The following list is a part of Critical Tracking Events that may be found in the supply chain of the Poly Products business.  7.5.2.1 Product creation/repacking 7.5.2.2 Origination (create a unique identifier – product enters supply chain) 7.5.2.3 Aggregation (bring discrete items together) 7.5.2.4 Disaggregation 7.5.2.5 Convert (repack or re-label) 7.5.2.6 Product receipt (at warehouse) 7.5.2.7 Product shipping  7.6 Key Data Elements 7.6.1 Key Data Elements are those data required to successfully trace a product and/or its ingredients through all relevant Critical Tracking Events.  7.6.2 Each Critical Tracking Event shall be carefully analyzed to ensure that sufficiently gritty data are collected to permit traceability.  7.6.3 The ability to trace product paths through the supply chain depends on logging Key Data Elements associated with these events.  7.7 Key Data Elements 7.7.1 Product records should follow a standardized format. The following are the key data elements that shall be made available for each material or finished product:  7.7.1.1 When (date/time) each lot was manufactured.  7.7.1.2 All ingredients (ink, film etc.) used in the manufacture of the product, along with their corresponding unique reference/batch/lot numbers (not item code).   7.8 Consumer Information 7.8.1 Provision of accurate and easy-to-understand information for consumers on appropriate handling procedures for food packaging products is important for minimizing the potential for foodborne illnesses caused by mishandling. | Daily | Sales & Marketing Manager, Quality Manager, Food Safety Team, Warehouse Suprvisor | Traceability Audit Report, RM/PM Inspection Records. |  |  |  |  |

| FS_PRP_14 | PRP for Food Packaging Information & Customer Communication | This PRP describes the basic requirements for food packaging, lot identification and traceability systems, listing the key data elements that should be available for each material, ingredient or finished product, and explaining the importance of consumer information to preventing foodborne illness caused by food packaging product mishandling. | Finished product must bear basic information concerning the product for the benefit of the consumer to prevent harm to his health from food consumption. | 7.1 Product Information and Consumer 7.1.1 Insufficient product information, and/or inadequate knowledge of general food hygiene, can lead to products being mishandled at later stages in the food chain.  7.1.2 Such mishandling can result in illness, or products becoming unsuitable for consumption, even where adequate hygiene control measures have been taken earlier in the food chain.  7.2 Codex Recommended Practices 7.2.1 Information on products from Poly Products Ltd complies with codex recommended practices. Products should bear appropriate information to ensure that:  7.2.2 Adequate and accessible information is available to the next person in the food chain to enable them to handle, store and display the product safely and correctly.  7.2.3 The lot or batch can be easily identified and recalled if necessary.   7.3 Lot Identification and Labelling 7.3.1 Lot identification is essential in product recall and also helps effective stock rotation.  7.3.2 Each food packaging is labelled to identify the Job Ticket number.  7.3.3 All products should be accompanied by or bear adequate information to enable the next person in the food chain to handle, display, store and use the product safely and correctly.  7.4 Product Tracing Systems 7.4.1 Product tracing and record keeping systems is in place to ensure products are traced through the supply chain.  7.4.2 Product tracing systems shall be implemented in a manner that records on the immediate sources (1-step back) of incoming raw materials and subsequent recipients (1-step forward) of finished products are collected. The Job Ticket No and name of the manufacturing facility shall appear on each case and/or pallet of product, including quantity.   7.5 Critical Tracking Events 7.5.1 Considering the entire food supply chain, there are several points in time and locations where data need to be collected to enable full product traceability.  7.5.2 These points have been termed to be “Critical Tracking Events.” The following list is a part of Critical Tracking Events that may be found in the supply chain of the Poly Products business.  7.5.2.1 Product creation/repacking 7.5.2.2 Origination (create a unique identifier – product enters supply chain) 7.5.2.3 Aggregation (bring discrete items together) 7.5.2.4 Disaggregation 7.5.2.5 Convert (repack or re-label) 7.5.2.6 Product receipt (at warehouse) 7.5.2.7 Product shipping  7.6 Key Data Elements 7.6.1 Key Data Elements are those data required to successfully trace a product and/or its ingredients through all relevant Critical Tracking Events.  7.6.2 Each Critical Tracking Event shall be carefully analyzed to ensure that sufficiently gritty data are collected to permit traceability.  7.6.3 The ability to trace product paths through the supply chain depends on logging Key Data Elements associated with these events.  7.7 Key Data Elements 7.7.1 Product records should follow a standardized format. The following are the key data elements that shall be made available for each material or finished product:  7.7.1.1 When (date/time) each lot was manufactured.  7.7.1.2 All ingredients (ink, film etc.) used in the manufacture of the product, along with their corresponding unique reference/batch/lot numbers (not item code).   7.8 Consumer Information 7.8.1 Provision of accurate and easy-to-understand information for consumers on appropriate handling procedures for food packaging products is important for minimizing the potential for foodborne illnesses caused by mishandling. | Daily | Sales & Marketing Manager, Quality Manager, Food Safety Team, Warehouse Suprvisor | Traceability Audit Report, RM/PM Inspection Records. |  |  |  |  |

Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. | 3 | Utilities | PRP for Utilities. | The PRP outlines the programmes that ensures that the organization is operating, maintaining and repairing components of the utility system to avoid contamination of products and to achieve efficiency in energy, water and air use. | 1.0 General Provisions 1.1 All factory buildings and facilities including utilities is managed in such a manner as to prevent contamination of products and processes. They are also managed in the most energy efficient manner without endangering the health and safety of employees.  1.2 Facilities Management will endeavour to take the necessary steps to provide an adequate, reliable, and cost-effective utilities infrastructure at all present and planned future buildings and facilities managed by the department. These shall be established in the most hygienic manner in order to ensure product safety.  1.3 The provision and distribution routes for utilities to and around processing and storage areas are designed to minimize the risk of product contamination. The quality of utilities is monitored to minimize product contamination risk.   2.0 Water Supply 2.1 Sufficient supply of potable water to meet the needs of production processes is assured. Facilities for storage and distribution of water have been designed to meet the quality requirements of water.  2.2 Poly Products uses water for washing and other cleaning activities. Potable water is sourced from the municipal water treatment plant. Approved water pipes have been used on site to connect water from the main municipal lines to preserve its quality and safety. Connections are hygienically done to prevent external contaminated water from flowing into the pipes in the event that water stops flowing from the treatment plant.  2.3 Periodic water analysis shall be done on an annual basis. See attachment FS/PRP 03/ATTACH 01 for the scope, frequency, sampling point etc. This activity is outsourced to the national laboratory or approved/recognized testing laboratory to carry out by taking water. The appropriate ISO method or other authorized standard for air count is employed in this exercise.   3.0 Air quality and ventilation 3.1 Air flowing from outside into the production space can be a source of bacteria and mould spores. Poly Products has considered this in the design of its ventilation system especially at the production hall. Hence there are no windows opening directly into the production areas.  3.2 Periodic air counts are done for each of the sections of production. See attachment FS/PRP 03/ATTACH 01 This activity is outsourced to the national laboratory or approved/recognized testing laboratory to carry out. Prepared media in petri dishes are exposed in various sections of production for some minutes. Dishes are incubated and the total viable count results are analyzed. The appropriate ISO method or other authorized standard for air count is employed in this exercise.   4.0 Compressed air and other gases 4.1 Compressed air (which are from in-built vacuum pumps) used in the production process have been constructed and maintained so as to prevent direct contact products and the packaging.  4.2 Maintenance of the compressed air system is part of the site maintenance schedule. Maintenance shall include checking and cleaning of filters and replacement of filters if necessary.   5.0 Lighting 5.1 Adequate lighting has been provided in all production and storage areas to allow personnel to operate in a hygienic manner.   5.2 All lights in both critical and non-critical areas are covered to catch fragments of glass in case of lamp breakage.   5.3 Maintenance work on lighting is done in such a way as to prevent contamination of products. results.question: What columns structure the HACCP verification plan?
results.expected_answer: Actions, Frequency, Responsible, Method used in verification, Record.
results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context, the HACCP verification plan is structured by the following columns:

* CCP No.
* Step
* Hazard description/Operation Defect
* Control measure(s)
* Targets
* Operational Limit
* Control Parameters
* Critical Limits
* Procedure (How)
* Frequency
* Responsibility
* Corrections
* Corrective actions
* Records
* Verification (details in Verification Plan)

results.question: What is our procedure for handling non-conforming raw material from an approved supplier? (cross-document)
results.expected_answer: Per HACCP PRP for Management of Purchased Materials: non-conforming items placed on-hold and rejected/returned to supplier (imported items sold to recyclers or destroyed under supervision); supplier notified and approval status reviewed.
results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents, here's the answer:

According to Source 3: Current HACCP MANUAL 3.10.2022 - Copy.xlsx, Sheet: MGT OF PURCH MAT & SERV, Section: MGT OF PURCH MAT & SERV (FS_PRP_06), our procedure for handling non-conforming raw material from an approved supplier is as follows:

1. All delivered materials are tested and/or covered by COA to verify conformity with specified requirements prior to acceptance or use.
2. Non-conforming products are placed on-hold and rejected, and the supplier is notified of the non-conformance.
3. In cases where purchased items are imported, the material is either sold to recycling plants in the case of packaging or destroyed under supervision in the case of other items which cannot be recycled.

Additionally, Source 5: Current HACCP MANUAL 3.10.2022 - Copy.xlsx, Sheet: REWORK, Section: REWORK (FS_PRP_11) provides further guidance on handling non-conforming raw materials:

1. In the case of quality parameters or suspected microbiological contamination, the product is taken through a segregation process to sort out the compliant material from those that cannot be used for production.
2. The non-conforming material that cannot be re-worked is affixed with a Reject label and scrapped by cutting into shreds so as to disfigure the materials before being disposed of.

Please note that these procedures are based on the provided context documents, and it's essential to verify them against any relevant regulations or industry standards.

This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place.
